conventions.convention: Finite nonempty state, action, and reward sets; stationary Markov policies; integer horizon H ≥ 1; discount 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1; fixed initial state s₀; common joint next-state/reward mass under target and behavior policies. AC is assumed for policy-induced path laws.
Logged data contain n ≥ 1 independent trajectories with behavior law and known true behavior propensities. Full horizon coverage is target-law absolute continuity with respect to behavior law.
W₀:ₜ includes actions 0 through t, and its prefix includes reward Rₜ₊₁ and state Sₜ₊₁. Weights are set to zero on behavior-null prefixes.
WIS returns zero when its total weight is zero. An observed zero behavior propensity with positive target propensity returns unsupported; a zero-over-zero ratio is set to zero.

DR Q functions and finite nonnegative multipliers are fixed during evaluation expectation, possibly conditional on independent training data. V̂ₜ averages Q̂ₜ under the target policy, and V̂_H is identically zero.

load_bearing.statement: A fixed logged dataset of size n ≥ 1 consists of independent trajectories, each with law Pᵘ_H for a behavior policy μ; the true behavior propensities are known. Full horizon coverage means Pᵖ_H ≪ Pᵘ_H. Policy laws have the stated products of action probabilities and common transition/reward masses.

Under AC, the finite-horizon dataset conditions, and full horizon coverage, each prefix policy-ratio product is a version of the target-prefix Radon–Nikodym derivative with respect to the behavior-prefix law. For every target-integrable real prefix function g, Eμ[W₀:ₜg] = Eπ[g] and Eμ[W₀:ₜ|g|] < ∞; this includes full-horizon functions.

Under AC and the stated finite-horizon dataset conditions, with fixed finite Q functions and multipliers, the DR sample average has expectation J_H(π;s₀) either when full coverage holds and multipliers are exact ratios on behavior-positive reachable pairs, or when the entire finite-horizon Q model is exact with zero terminal value. The exact-model branch requires neither coverage nor correct multipliers.

Under AC, full trajectory coverage, known true behavior propensities, and the finite-horizon dataset conditions, numerical outputs of the importance-sampling algorithm are finite, unsupported occurs only on a null event, and OIS and PDIS each have expectation J_H(π;s₀) after any fixed finite extension there. No finite-sample WIS unbiasedness is asserted.

The two specified finite one-step MDPs have identical behavior-data laws at every sample size but target values 1 and −1 and different unique optimal initial actions. No real-valued data estimator can be unbiased in both, and no data-based action selector can identify the unique optimum with certainty in both.

published_dependencies.used_for: Direction of coverage: behavior-null events must be target-null.
Explicit inherited AC hypothesis for path-law, RN, and conditional-expectation suppliers.
Target values and expectations under identical logged-data laws.
Absolute integrability and subtraction of finite positive and negative integrals.
Trajectory probability measures have total mass one.
Density is an almost-everywhere equivalence class rather than a distinguished pointwise function.
Factoring prefix densities through finite counting measure, with a common finite exhaustion.
Nonnegative substitution applied separately to positive and negative parts.
Finite reward sums, estimator averages, and DR telescoping.
RN existence and uniqueness for finite prefix measures under AC.
Almost-sure interpretation of DR conditional residual identities.
Event-integral characterization of conditional expectations on finite history sigma-algebras.
Linearity and preservation of total expectation in the exact-model DR branch.
Existence under AC without a completeness assumption.
Pulling the bounded history-measurable cumulative multiplier out of conditional expectation.

concerns.concern: Verification 1.1 writes V̂₀(s₀) = ½Q̂₀(s₀,a) + ½Q̂₀(s₀,b). The Example specifies a target policy choosing b deterministically, and alg-doubly-robust-ope defines V̂ using target probabilities, so the defining average is 0·Q̂₀(s₀,a) + 1·Q̂₀(s₀,b). Both fitted Q values are zero here, so the displayed equality and resulting score remain numerically true, but the coefficients incorrectly use the behavior policy.
